newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury seeks longer-term funding for IRS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury seeks longer-term funding for IRS.

text.p: The Internal Revenue Service needs longer-term funding to systematically update its information technology and avoid problems like it now has, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Thursday.
"Today, the IRS operates in a low-trust, short-tether budgeting environment," Summers said in testimony prepared for delivery to the Senate committee on government affairs.
"As we re-establish trust and demonstrate that the IRS is investing resources wisely and prudently, we are examining longer term approaches to budgeting," he added.
Summers said Treasury was asking for funding for two years for the tax-collecting IRS to buy new computers and other capital goods needed for a more modern system.

The proposed longer-term funding is part of a five-part plan that Summers previously outlined for making the IRS more efficient. Summers said the IRS' problems -- from protecting taxpayers' privacy to making sure telephones are answered -- have developed over decades and will take time to fix.
Steady improvements in service by banks, brokers and credit card companies "bring ever more sharply into focus the IRS' problems with customer service," Summers acknowledged.
He noted that the IRS collects 95 percent of all government revenues and reminded Congress that it came from a tax system that depends upon voluntary compliance by taxpayers.
"Therefore all of us must act responsibly and deliberately as we introduce and instill change and recognize that these changes will not bear fruit instantly," Summers said.
